requirements.message: Some values in the coordinate_system column of *_electrodes.tsv are not present as space entities in *_coordsystem.json files.

issue.message:
Some values in the coordinate_system column of *_electrodes.tsv are not present as
space entities in *_coordsystem.json files.

ai_enrichment.description: Values in the coordinate_system column of an electrodes.tsv do not appear as space entities in the corresponding coordsystem files.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Each coordinate system named in the table must have a coordinate system file declaring it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The column names which system each electrode's coordinates are expressed in. If no file declares that system, the coordinates cannot be interpreted.
common_causes: A coordinate system is named in the table but no matching coordsystem file exists.
The space entity in the coordsystem filename is spelled differently from the column value.
The electrodes table was written against a different set of coordinate system files.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: List the distinct values in the coordinate_system column and confirm each has a coordsystem file whose space entity matches exactly, including case. Add the missing files or correct the spelling so the two agree.

title: ERROR EMG_COORD_SYS_PARENTS
summary: EMG_COORD_SYS_PARENTS: Some parent coordinate systems were not found.

requirements.message: Some parent coordinate systems were not found.

issue.message: Some parent coordinate systems were not found.

ai_enrichment.description: A coordinate system refers to a parent coordinate system that was not found.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Coordinate systems can be defined relative to others, and the chain must resolve.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A coordinate system defined relative to a parent has no absolute meaning until the parent is found. A broken chain leaves the positions uninterpretable even though they are present.
common_causes: The parent coordinate system file is missing from the dataset.
The parent is named with a different spelling than the file declaring it.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Identify the parent coordinate system named in the definition and confirm a file declares it. Add the missing definition or correct the name so the chain resolves.

title: WARNING EMPTY_DATASET_NAME
summary: EMPTY_DATASET_NAME: The Name field of dataset_description.json is present but empty of visible characters.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EMPTY_DATASET_NAME (warning). The Name field of dataset_description.json is present but empty of visible characters. When path == '/dataset_description.json' and type(json.Name) != 'null', it requires that match(json.Name, '\S'). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named EmptyDatasetName in the BIDS schema. It concerns hints data.

requirements.message: The Name field of dataset_description.json is present but empty of visible characters.

issue.message: The Name field of dataset_description.json is present but empty of visible characters.

ai_enrichment.description: The Name field of dataset_description.json is present but contains no visible characters.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The required field is technically there, so the structure is satisfied, but it carries no information.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The dataset name is how the dataset is identified in listings, in repositories and in the outputs of tools that report which dataset they processed. An empty name means every one of those shows a blank.
common_causes: A template dataset_description.json was created and the name was never filled in.
The field holds only whitespace.
An automated step wrote an empty string as a placeholder.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Set Name to a short descriptive title for the study. It should be recognisable on its own, since it will appear away from any other context.

title: WARNING EOG_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH
summary: EOG_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH: The EOGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type EOG in the associated channels.tsv file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EOG_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH (warning). The EOGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type EOG in the associated channels.tsv file. When the file's suffix is eeg and type(sidecar.EOGChannelCount) != "null" and associations.channels.type, it requires that sidecar.EOGChannelCount == the number of associations.channels.type, "EOG". Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named EOGChannelCountReq in the BIDS schema. It concerns eeg data.

requirements.message: The EOGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type EOG in the associated channels.tsv file.

issue.message:
The EOGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels
with type EOG in the associated channels.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: The EOGChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is EOG. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many EOG channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset is still valid BIDS, but one of the two statements about the recording is wrong and downstream software may read either of them. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while EOGChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original EOGChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar EOGChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "eog" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as EOG.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals EOG. If that number is right, set EOGChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

title: ERROR EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS
summary: EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS (error). EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values. When the file is in the fmap datatype directory and the file's suffix is epi and "bval" in associations, it requires that min(associations.bval.values) < 100. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named EPISmallBVals in the BIDS schema. It concerns fmap data.

requirements.message: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.

issue.message: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.

ai_enrichment.description: An EPI fieldmap has associated b-values, but none of them is small. A fieldmap acquisition used for distortion correction should include at least one low b-value volume, below 100.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The presence of b-values means the acquisition is diffusion-weighted, and distortion correction needs an essentially undiffusion-weighted volume to work from.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Registration between the fieldmap and the data being corrected relies on anatomical contrast. Strongly diffusion-weighted volumes have little of it and low signal-to-noise, so a fieldmap consisting only of high b-value volumes cannot be registered reliably.
common_causes: Only diffusion-weighted volumes were included when the fieldmap was assembled.
The b-zero volumes were separated into a different file.
The b-value file belongs to a different acquisition.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Include the low b-value volumes in the fieldmap acquisition, or use the acquisition that contains them. Check that the .bval file really corresponds to this file, since a mismatched b-value file is a common cause.

title: WARNING EVENTS_TSV_MISSING
summary: EVENTS_TSV_MISSING: Task scans should have a corresponding 'events.tsv' file. If this is a resting state scan you can ignore this warning or rename the task to include the word "rest".
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EVENTS_TSV_MISSING (warning). Task scans should have a corresponding 'events.tsv' file. If this is a resting state scan you can ignore this warning or rename the task to include the word "rest". When dataset.dataset_description.DatasetType == "raw" and datatype != "beh" and "task" in entities and !entities.task matches rest and ![suffix] shares a value with ["events", "beh", "channels", "electrodes", "optodes"] and extension != ".json" and datatype != "meg" or entities.subject != "emptyroom" and entities.task != "noise", it requires that "events" in associations. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named EventsMissing in the BIDS schema. It concerns events data.

requirements.message: Task scans should have a corresponding 'events.tsv' file. If this is a resting state scan you can ignore this warning or rename the task to include the word "rest".

issue.message:
Task scans should have a corresponding 'events.tsv' file.
If this is a resting state scan you can ignore this warning or rename the task to include the word "rest".

ai_enrichment.description: A scan with a task entity has no corresponding events.tsv file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, and whether it matters depends entirely on the task. For a task with discrete trials it is a real omission. For a resting-state run, which has a task entity by convention but no events, it is expected and can be ignored.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An events file is what makes a task run analysable: it says what happened and when. Without it, a task dataset records that something was done to the participant but not what. Timing information is also difficult to reconstruct later, since it lives in the stimulus software's logs rather than in the imaging data.
common_causes: The run is resting state, conventionally named with a task entity such as task-rest, and genuinely has no events. This is the most common case and needs no action.
Stimulus presentation logs were never converted into an events.tsv.
The events file exists but its entities do not match the recording exactly, so it is not paired.
The events file sits in the wrong directory.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Decide first whether the run has events at all. If it is resting state, ignore the warning. If it has a task, convert the stimulus software's log into an events.tsv with at minimum the onset and duration columns, onsets measured in seconds from the first stored data point. If a file already exists, check that its entities match the recording exactly, since an events file is paired with its recording by name.

title: WARNING EVENT_ONSET_ORDER
summary: EVENT_ONSET_ORDER: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EVENT_ONSET_ORDER (warning). The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted. When the file's suffix is events and the file extension is .tsv, it requires that allequal(sorted(columns.onset, "numeric"), columns.onset). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named SortedOnsets in the BIDS schema. It concerns events data.

requirements.message: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.

issue.message: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.

ai_enrichment.description: The onset column of an events.tsv is not sorted in increasing order.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The standard recommends events be listed in the order they occurred, which makes the file readable and matches what most tools assume.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Some software reads events sequentially and assumes chronological order. More practically, an unsorted file is hard to inspect by eye, and out-of-order onsets often indicate that rows from different conditions or different runs were concatenated without being merged properly.
common_causes: The file was assembled by concatenating one block of rows per condition rather than merging by time.
The file was sorted by trial type, or by another column, before being saved.
Rows from two runs were combined.
A correction added rows at the end rather than in place.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Sort the rows by the onset column. Before doing so, check why they were out of order: if two runs were concatenated, sorting merges them into one timeline, which is not a fix. Onsets must be measured from the start of the recording the file belongs to.

title: WARNING EXCESSIVE_COORDSYSTEM_SPECIFICITY
summary: EXCESSIVE_COORDSYSTEM_SPECIFICITY: Task, acquisition or run entities detected in coordsystem.tsv. Coordinate systems should generally not vary within a session. Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create new sessions when multiple coordinate systems are appropriate.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EXCESSIVE_COORDSYSTEM_SPECIFICITY (warning). Task, acquisition or run entities detected in coordsystem.tsv. Coordinate systems should generally not vary within a session. Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create new sessions when multiple coordinate systems are appropriate. When the file's suffix is coordsystem and the file extension is .json, it requires that !("task" in entities) and !("acquisition" in entities) and !("run" in entities). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named CoordsystemSpecificity in the BIDS schema. It concerns channels data.

requirements.message: Task, acquisition or run entities detected in coordsystem.tsv. Coordinate systems should generally not vary within a session. Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create new sessions when multiple coordinate systems are appropriate.

expression: !("task" in entities) AND !("acquisition" in entities) AND !("run" in entities)

issue.message:
Task, acquisition or run entities detected in coordsystem.tsv.
Coordinate systems should generally not vary within a session.
Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create new
sessions when multiple coordinate systems are appropriate.

ai_enrichment.description: A coordsystem.json filename carries task, acquisition or run entities. Coordinate systems do not normally vary between runs.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about scope, with the same reasoning as an over-specified electrodes file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A coordinate system is a property of how positions were measured, not of an individual recording. Scoping it to one run forces duplication across the others, and duplicates drift.
common_causes: The file was generated per recording by a conversion that copies entities.
Entities copied from the data file without considering scope.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Remove the task, acquisition and run entities so the file applies to every recording that shares the coordinate system, and let inheritance do the rest.

Electrode definitions should generally not vary within a session. Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create a new session each time electrodes are reconfigured. When the file's suffix is electrodes and the file extension is .tsv, it requires that !("task" in entities) and !("acquisition" in entities) and !("run" in entities). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named ElectrodeSpecificity in the BIDS schema. It concerns channels data.

requirements.message: Task, acquisition or run entities detected in electrodes.tsv. Electrode definitions should generally not vary within a session. Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create a new session each time electrodes are reconfigured.

expression: !("task" in entities) AND !("acquisition" in entities) AND !("run" in entities)

issue.message:
Task, acquisition or run entities detected in electrodes.tsv.
Electrode definitions should generally not vary within a session.
Consider removing the excess entity/entities or create a new
session each time electrodes are reconfigured.

ai_enrichment.description: An electrodes.tsv filename carries task, acquisition or run entities. Electrode positions rarely change between runs, so this level of specificity is usually unintended.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about file placement rather than content. The positions may be perfectly correct while being scoped more narrowly than they need to be.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A file named with a run entity applies only to that run. If the electrodes did not move, the same positions then have to be duplicated for every run, and duplicated files drift apart when one is corrected and the others are not.
common_causes: The electrodes file was generated per recording by a conversion that copies the recording's entities.
The entities were copied from the data file without considering scope.
The electrodes genuinely were re-placed between runs, which is unusual.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Unless the electrodes genuinely moved, remove the task, acquisition and run entities from the electrodes filename so that one file covers every recording it applies to. Inheritance will then apply it to all of them. If positions really did change between runs, keeping the entities is correct and the warning can be left.

title: ERROR FIELDMAP_WITHOUT_MAGNITUDE_FILE
summary: FIELDMAP_WITHOUT_MAGNITUDE_FILE: 'fieldmap.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude.nii[.gz]' file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code FIELDMAP_WITHOUT_MAGNITUDE_FILE (error). 'fieldmap.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude.nii[.gz]' file. When the file's suffix is fieldmap and match(extension, '\.nii(\.gz)?$'), it requires that "magnitude" in associations. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named FmapFieldmapWithoutMagnitude in the BIDS schema. It concerns fmap data.

requirements.message: 'fieldmap.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude.nii[.gz]' file.

issue.message: 'fieldmap.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude.nii[.gz]' file.

ai_enrichment.description: A fieldmap image has no associated magnitude image.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. A fieldmap describes the field offset at each voxel but carries no anatomical contrast, so on its own it cannot be aligned to the images it is meant to correct.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correction requires registering the fieldmap to the distorted data. That registration is driven by the magnitude image, which shows anatomy. Without it, the fieldmap cannot be placed in the right space and is unusable.
common_causes: The magnitude image was not converted, often because the source series was not recognised.
The magnitude image was converted but named so that it does not pair with the fieldmap.
Only part of the fieldmap acquisition was copied into the dataset.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Look in the source data for the magnitude series belonging to this fieldmap and convert it. The magnitude file must sit in the same fmap directory and carry the same entities as the fieldmap, differing only in suffix, or the two will not be recognised as a pair.

title: ERROR FLIP_ANGLE_NOT_MATCHING_ASLCONTEXT_TSV

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in FlipAngle does not match the number of volumes listed in the associated aslcontext.tsv. FlipAngle holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error: the dataset is not valid BIDS until the lengths match. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than FlipAngle has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in FlipAngle, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: The gzip header of a compressed file contains a non-empty comment field. Gzip stores a free-text comment alongside the compressed data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning with two distinct meanings, and it is worth working out which applies. It may be a disclosure risk, because the header can carry information from the machine where the file was compressed. It may also simply indicate that the file was not compressed reproducibly, so byte-identical inputs produce different files.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Gzip headers are not visible in any normal view of a dataset, so a free-text comment can travel with a shared file without anyone noticing. The same fields also prevent checksums from matching between two compressions of identical data, which breaks verification and deduplication.
common_causes: The file was compressed with a tool that records source metadata by default, which most command-line gzip implementations do.
The file was compressed as a separate step rather than written compressed by the conversion tool.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Recompress the file with the comment field suppressed. Most gzip implementations offer an option for this, and libraries that write compressed data directly usually leave these fields empty already. Before recompressing, check whether the existing comment field discloses anything sensitive, since that determines how urgent this is.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: This finding is about the compression container, not about the data inside it. Decompressing and recompressing changes nothing about the image or table the file holds.

ai_enrichment.description: An iEEG data file has no associated electrodes.tsv.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. For intracranial recordings, electrode positions are not supplementary information, they are what identifies the recording sites.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Intracranial electrode placement is determined by clinical need and differs for every participant. Without positions, a channel name is an arbitrary label and there is no way to know what was recorded from where, which makes the recording uninterpretable and impossible to combine across participants.
common_causes: Electrode positions were not localised, or were not exported into the dataset.
The electrodes file exists but its entities do not match the recording.
The file is placed where it cannot be inherited by the recording that needs it.

A single electrodes file may serve several recordings from the same implantation: place it at the session level with the entities shared by those recordings, and inheritance will apply it to all of them.

ai_enrichment.description: LabelingDuration carries a value greater than 10 seconds. BIDS expresses this field in seconds, and a genuine LabelingDuration above 10 seconds seconds is rare enough that the validator asks you to confirm it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, not an error: the dataset is still valid BIDS and the validator cannot tell a real long value from a unit mistake. It is flagging that the number looks like milliseconds. For most acquisitions LabelingDuration falls between roughly 0.5 and 2 seconds for arterial spin labelling.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Timing metadata is read by analysis software as seconds without further checking. A value that is 1000 times too large silently distorts anything derived from it, including slice timing correction, temporal filtering, design matrices and modelling of the haemodynamic response. Nothing downstream will warn you a second time.
example_scenarios: A converter copies LabelingDuration from DICOM unchanged, so a sidecar records the value in milliseconds where BIDS expects seconds.
common_causes: The value was copied straight from a DICOM header or scanner console in milliseconds. BIDS requires seconds, so the number is 1000 times too large.
A conversion script wrote LabelingDuration without applying the unit conversion its source format needed.
The field was filled in by hand from a scanner protocol printout, which usually reports milliseconds.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the value against the acquisition protocol. If it was taken from a DICOM header in milliseconds, divide by 1000 and write the result back into the JSON sidecar. If the long value is genuinely correct for this acquisition, leave it as it is: the warning is a prompt to verify, not a defect to remove, and there is no way to suppress it other than correcting the value.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS states all timing metadata in seconds. Most sources of the same information, DICOM in particular, state it in milliseconds, so this class of mistake is common and worth checking across every timing field in the sidecar rather than only the one reported.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in LabelingDuration does not match the fourth dimension of the NIfTI header. LabelingDuration holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error: the dataset is not valid BIDS until the lengths match. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than LabelingDuration has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in LabelingDuration, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in LabelingDuration does not match the number of volumes listed in the associated aslcontext.tsv. LabelingDuration holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error: the dataset is not valid BIDS until the lengths match. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than LabelingDuration has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in LabelingDuration, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: M0Type is set to "separate", which declares that the dataset contains a standalone m0scan, but no associated m0scan.nii[.gz] and m0scan.json were found.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The declaration and the files disagree: the sidecar promises a separate M0 image that is not there.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The M0 image provides the equilibrium magnetisation that ASL quantification divides by to convert the perfusion-weighted signal into cerebral blood flow. Without it, quantification cannot proceed or falls back to an assumed value, which changes every perfusion estimate.
common_causes: The M0 series was not converted into the dataset.
The m0scan file is present but its entities do not match the ASL recording, so the two are not paired.
The M0 volume is actually included within the ASL time series, in which case M0Type should be "included" rather than "separate".
The M0 image was placed in the wrong directory.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Establish where the M0 information really is. If a separate M0 series was acquired, convert it and place it in the perf directory with entities matching the ASL recording, alongside its own JSON sidecar. If the M0 volume is part of the ASL time series and listed in aslcontext.tsv, set M0Type to "included" instead. If no M0 was acquired at all, the correct value depends on how quantification is intended to proceed, and the other permitted values cover an estimated value or its absence.

ai_enrichment.description: The MAGNChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is MAGN. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many MAGN channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, so the dataset is not valid BIDS until the two agree. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while MAGNChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original MAGNChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar MAGNChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "magn" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as MAGN.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals MAGN. If that number is right, set MAGNChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

ai_enrichment.description: The MatrixSize metadata of a magnetic resonance spectroscopy file does not match the first three dimensions of the NIfTI header.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The metadata and the image header state the same spatial extent and disagree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: For spectroscopy, the spatial dimensions determine how voxels are laid out relative to anatomy. A mismatch means the metadata describes a different acquisition geometry than the file contains, so spectra cannot be placed reliably.
common_causes: The sidecar was copied from an acquisition with a different matrix.
The image was reshaped or resampled after the sidecar was written.
The dimensions were written in a different order than the header uses.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the first three dimensions from the NIfTI header and compare them against MatrixSize. Check the ordering before assuming the values are wrong, since a transposed but otherwise correct triple is a common cause. Correct whichever does not match the acquisition.

title: ERROR MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY
summary: MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY: ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY (error). ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar. When the file is in the mrs datatype directory and type(nifti_header.mrs) != "null", it requires that sidecar.ResonantNucleus == nifti_header.mrs.ResonantNucleus and sidecar.SpectrometerFrequency == nifti_header.mrs.SpectrometerFrequency. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named MRSNiftiConsistency in the BIDS schema. It concerns mrs data.

requirements.message: ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.

issue.message:
ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent
between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.

ai_enrichment.description: The ResonantNucleus or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the JSON sidecar and the NIfTI-MRS header extension.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Spectroscopy data carries these parameters in two places, and they disagree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The resonant nucleus and the spectrometer frequency together set the frequency axis of every spectrum. If they are inconsistent, chemical shifts are computed against the wrong reference, so peaks are assigned to the wrong metabolites.
common_causes: The sidecar was written by hand or from a template rather than from the data.
The sidecar was copied from an acquisition on a different scanner or with a different nucleus.
A conversion wrote the header extension and the sidecar from different sources.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Take the values from the NIfTI-MRS header extension, which is written directly from the acquisition, and make the sidecar agree with it unless you have specific reason to believe the extension is wrong. Confirm the nucleus matches the acquisition, since a proton acquisition described as another nucleus shifts the whole frequency axis.

title: ERROR MULTIPLE_README_FILES
summary: MULTIPLE_README_FILES: There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MULTIPLE_README_FILES (error). There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist. When match(path, '^/README.*'), it requires that exists(["README", "README.md", "README.rst", "README.txt"], "dataset") == 1. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named DuplicateReadmes in the BIDS schema. It concerns general data.

requirements.message: There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.

issue.message:
There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS
dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.

ai_enrichment.description: More than one README file is present at the dataset root, differing only in extension.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The dataset must have exactly one README, so that there is no question which one describes it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Two READMEs are two descriptions of the same dataset with no rule saying which is current. In practice one is usually an abandoned draft, and a reader has no way to tell which.
common_causes: A README was converted from one format to another and the original was left behind.
Two people added a README in different formats.
A template README was left in place alongside the real one.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Decide which file is current, merge anything worth keeping from the other into it, and delete the rest. Keep exactly one file named README, with at most one of the permitted extensions.

title: WARNING NIFTI_DIMENSION
summary: NIFTI_DIMENSION: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_DIMENSION (warning). NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short. When type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that the length of nifti_header.shape > 0 and min(nifti_header.shape) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiDimension in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.

issue.message: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.

ai_enrichment.description: The dimension field of the NIfTI header is blank or shorter than the image requires, so the header does not fully describe the image's shape.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The image data may be intact while the header fails to describe it, which means tools have to guess.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Voxel data in a NIfTI file is a flat block of numbers. Only the header says how to fold it into a volume. An underspecified dimension field means different readers may fold it differently.
common_causes: The file was written by a tool that did not populate the header fully.
The header was edited or copied from another image.
The image was produced by a conversion from a format that carries less geometry information.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original source data if possible, since a conversion tool that reads the source geometry will write a complete header. If the image cannot be re-converted, set the dimension fields explicitly using a NIfTI toolkit, taking the values from the acquisition protocol rather than guessing.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY
summary: NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY: The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.
retrieval_text:
Validation issue code NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY (warning). The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate. When type(nifti_header.axis_codes) != "null" and [entities.direction] shares a value with ["AP", "PA", "RL", "LR", "SI", "IS"] and sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection, it requires that entities.direction[2 - the length of sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection]
== nifti_header.axis_codes[index(["i", "j", "k"], sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection[0])]. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPEDir in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.

issue.message:
The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate
that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.

ai_enrichment.description: The PhaseEncodingDirection in the sidecar and the image's own orientation imply a phase-encoding axis that does not match the value of the dir entity in the filename.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about a disagreement between the filename and the metadata. Two independent statements are being made about the same fact and they do not agree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Susceptibility distortion correction reverses distortion along the phase-encoding axis and relies on knowing its direction. Getting the direction wrong does not fail: it applies the correction backwards, roughly doubling the distortion it was meant to remove.
common_causes: The dir entity was assigned by hand or by convention rather than derived from the acquisition, and does not match the data.
PhaseEncodingDirection was copied from another acquisition with the opposite polarity, which is easy in a pair of opposed-polarity scans.
The image orientation differs from what the converter assumed when it translated the scanner's axis convention.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Establish which acquisition each file really is by returning to the source data or the protocol, then make the filename and the sidecar agree with it. In an opposed-polarity pair, confirm the two files are not swapped, since that is the usual cause and it makes both files wrong at once.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PIXDIM
summary: NIFTI_PIXDIM: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_PIXDIM (warning). NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels. When suffix != 'pet' and type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that min(nifti_header.voxel_sizes) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPixdim in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.

issue.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.

ai_enrichment.description: The NIfTI header reports voxel sizes of zero. A voxel with no extent cannot describe a real image.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about the header rather than the voxel data. The image may display correctly while carrying no usable information about scale.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Voxel size is how anatomical distance is recovered from array indices. With zero voxel sizes, spatial smoothing, registration, volume measurement and any report in millimetres are all either impossible or wrong.
common_causes: The writing tool left the voxel size fields unset.
A header was constructed by hand or copied from an incompatible image.
A conversion from a source format that did not expose voxel dimensions.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original data, which is the reliable fix because the source carries the true voxel geometry. Only if that is impossible, set the voxel dimensions from the acquisition protocol with a NIfTI toolkit, and record that the geometry was reconstructed rather than read.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET
summary: NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET (warning). NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes. When the file's suffix is pet and type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that min([nifti_header.pixdim[1], nifti_header.pixdim[2], nifti_header.pixdim[3]]) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPixdimPET in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.

issue.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.

ai_enrichment.description: A PET image reports voxel sizes of zero along its spatial axes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning with the same meaning as a zero voxel size in any other image, reported separately because PET images are checked only on their spatial axes.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Quantitative PET analysis depends on knowing the volume each voxel represents. Without voxel sizes, concentrations, regional statistics and any coregistration with an anatomical image are unreliable.
common_causes: The reconstruction or conversion did not carry voxel geometry into the NIfTI header.
The image was converted from a format whose geometry was not read correctly.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original reconstruction output using a tool that reads its geometry. If the image must be repaired in place, take the voxel sizes from the reconstruction parameters, not from a similar scan.

title: WARNING NIFTI_UNIT
summary: NIFTI_UNIT: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_UNIT (warning). NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified. When type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that nifti_header.xyzt_units.xyz != 'unknown' and nifti_header.dim[0] < 4 or nifti_header.xyzt_units.t != 'unknown'. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiUnit in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.

issue.message: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.

ai_enrichment.description: The NIfTI header does not fully specify the units for the spatial and temporal dimensions.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. Readers will apply a default, usually millimetres and seconds, which is normally right but is an assumption rather than a fact the file states.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: If an image was written in different units and the header does not say so, every spatial measurement taken from it is wrong by a constant factor, and nothing in the file reveals it.
common_causes: The writing tool left the units field unset.
A conversion that did not propagate unit information.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Set the units field with a NIfTI toolkit after confirming what the image actually uses, or re-convert from source. Before doing either, check that the voxel sizes are plausible when read as millimetres, since that is the assumption everything downstream is already making.

title: ERROR NIRS_CHANNEL_COUNT

ai_enrichment.description: The NIRSChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is NIRS. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many NIRS channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, so the dataset is not valid BIDS until the two agree. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while NIRSChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original NIRSChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar NIRSChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "nirs" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as NIRS.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals NIRS. If that number is right, set NIRSChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: NIRS channel types begin with NIRS, for example NIRSCWAMPLITUDE. The count covers every channel whose type starts with that prefix, not only an exact match on the word NIRS.

title: WARNING NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS
summary: NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS (warning). NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file. When the file's suffix is nirs and the file extension is .snirf, it requires that associations.channels != null. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named RecommendedChannels in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

requirements.message: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.

issue.message: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: A NIRS recording has no associated channels.tsv file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the standard recommends rather than requires the file here. In practice a NIRS recording is difficult to use without it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: NIRS channels are source-detector pairs at specific wavelengths. Which pair and which wavelength a channel corresponds to is not recoverable from the data file alone, so without channels.tsv the channels cannot be related to positions on the head.
common_causes: The file was not exported alongside the recording.
Its entities do not match the recording, so the two are not paired.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add a channels.tsv beside the recording listing every channel with its name, type, wavelength and the source and detector it connects, together with the sampling frequency if it varies per channel.

title: ERROR NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY
summary: NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY: Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY (error). Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv. When the file's suffix is nirs and sidecar.SamplingFrequency == "n/a", it requires that associations.channels.sampling_frequency != null. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named NASamplingFreq in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

requirements.message: Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv.

issue.message:
Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency
column of channels.tsv.

ai_enrichment.description: The sampling frequency of a NIRS recording is not defined. It must be given either in the JSON sidecar or as a sampling_frequency column in channels.tsv.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. NIRS allows the sampling frequency to be stated per channel, because channels can be sampled at different rates, but one of the two forms must be present.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Without a sampling frequency, the samples cannot be placed in time at all. Nothing about the recording's timing, including the alignment of events to data, can be determined.
common_causes: The field was omitted from the sidecar and no per-channel column was provided.
Channels are sampled at different rates so no single value was written, but the per-channel column was not added either.
The value was written under a different field name.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add SamplingFrequency to the JSON sidecar if every channel shares one rate. If rates differ between channels, add a sampling_frequency column to channels.tsv giving the rate for each. Take the values from the acquisition software rather than inferring them from the data length.

title: WARNING NOSUBJECT_FOLDERS
summary: NOSUBJECT_FOLDERS: There should be no subject directories (labeled "sub-*") in the root of this study BIDS dataset.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NOSUBJECT_FOLDERS (warning). There should be no subject directories (labeled "sub-*") in the root of this study BIDS dataset. When path == '/dataset_description.json' and dataset.dataset_description.DatasetType == "study", it requires that the length of dataset.subjects.sub_dirs == 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NoSubjectFolders in the BIDS schema. It concerns dataset data.

requirements.message: There should be no subject directories (labeled "sub-*") in the root of this study BIDS dataset.

issue.message: There should be no subject directories (labeled "sub-*") in the root of this study BIDS dataset.

ai_enrichment.description: Subject directories were found at the root of a directory that is not expected to contain them, for example a derivatives or sourcedata directory being treated as a study root.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about where subject directories appear relative to the dataset they belong to.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The location of subject directories determines which dataset they belong to. Misplaced, the same data can be counted twice, or a derivative dataset can be mistaken for raw data.
common_causes: A derivatives dataset placed without its own dataset_description.json.
Nested datasets where the boundary between them is not marked.
Subject directories left at a level that the standard reserves for something else.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the directory layout against the structure the standard defines for this kind of dataset. A derivatives dataset needs its own dataset_description.json declaring it as a derivative; without one, its subject directories are read as part of the parent dataset.

title: ERROR PARTICIPANT_ID_MISMATCH
summary: PARTICIPANT_ID_MISMATCH: Subject directories found in this dataset did not match the values in the participant_id column found in the participants.tsv file.
retrieval_text:
Validation issue code PARTICIPANT_ID_MISMATCH (error). Subject directories found in this dataset did not match the values in the participant_id column found in the participants.tsv file. When path == '/participants.tsv', it requires that allequal(
  sorted(columns.participant_id shares a value with dataset.subjects.sub_dirs),
  sorted(dataset.subjects.sub_dirs)
). Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named ParticipantIDMismatch in the BIDS schema. It concerns dataset data.

requirements.message: Subject directories found in this dataset did not match the values in the participant_id column found in the participants.tsv file.

issue.message:
Subject directories found in this dataset did not match the values in
the participant_id column found in the participants.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: The subject directories present in the dataset do not match the values in the participant_id column of participants.tsv.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. participants.tsv is the dataset's own list of who is in it, and it disagrees with what is actually on disk. The mismatch can run either way: a listed participant with no directory, or a directory with no row.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: participants.tsv is where demographic and group information lives. If the identifiers do not line up, that information is attached to the wrong person or to nobody, which can silently misassign group membership in an analysis. It is also a common symptom of a partially copied dataset.
example_scenarios: participants.tsv lists 01, 02 and 03 while the directories are named sub-01, sub-02 and sub-03. The column needs the sub- prefix on every row.
common_causes: A participant was excluded and their directory removed, without the participants.tsv row being removed, or the reverse.
The participant_id values omit the sub- prefix. The column must contain the full directory name, such as sub-01, not the bare label.
Zero-padding differs between the table and the directories, so sub-1 and sub-01 do not match.
Only part of the dataset was copied, so directories are missing for participants that are legitimately listed.
Trailing whitespace in the column, which is invisible in a spreadsheet but makes the strings unequal.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: List the subject directories and compare them against the participant_id column. Check the prefix and the zero-padding first, since those account for most mismatches and affect every row at once. Then reconcile the genuine differences: add rows for participants that exist, remove rows for participants that do not, and confirm no rows were lost when the file was last edited.

title: WARNING PDT2_ECHOS_SHOULD_MATCH_NIFTI_LENGTH
summary: PDT2_ECHOS_SHOULD_MATCH_NIFTI_LENGTH: The EchoTime parameter for _PDT2.nii[.gz] files should have one value per volume.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code PDT2_ECHOS_SHOULD_MATCH_NIFTI_LENGTH (warning). The EchoTime parameter for _PDT2.nii[.gz] files should have one value per volume. When the file's suffix is PDT2 and sidecar.EchoTime != null and the image has exactly 4 dimensions, it requires that type(sidecar.EchoTime) == 'array' and the length of sidecar.EchoTime == nifti_header.dim[4]. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named PDT2Echos in the BIDS schema. It concerns anat data.

requirements.message: The EchoTime parameter for _PDT2.nii[.gz] files should have one value per volume.

issue.message:
The EchoTime parameter for _PDT2.nii[.gz] files should have one value
per volume.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in EchoTime does not match the number of volumes in the PDT2 image. EchoTime holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset remains valid BIDS, but the mismatch usually indicates a real bookkeeping mistake. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.

ai_enrichment.description: Both orientation codes in the NIfTI header, sform_code and qform_code, are zero, so the file declares no relationship between its voxel grid and any anatomical coordinate system.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, and it is one of the more consequential ones. The image has no stated orientation at all, so nothing can determine which side is left.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Left and right are not recoverable from voxel data. When both orientation codes are zero, software falls back to its own assumption, and different tools assume differently. A left-right flip introduced this way survives into every result and is essentially undetectable in a brain image, which makes it one of the few errors capable of reversing a lateralised finding without anyone noticing.

A conversion from a format that did not carry orientation information.
A header was stripped deliberately, sometimes as a misguided anonymisation step.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original source data, which is the only route that recovers the true orientation. If that is impossible, the orientation must be established from external evidence, for example a scan with known laterality or a marker visible in the image, and not assumed. Record how it was determined. Do not simply set an orientation code to a plausible value, because that replaces an honest absence of information with a confident claim that may be wrong.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Of the two, sform is the one most analysis software reads. Both being zero is the worst case; one being set is usually workable.
