You must provide enough metadata to determine the TotalReadoutTime of this file.
`TotalReadoutTime` or `EffectiveEchoSpacing` satisfy this criterion.

ai_enrichment.description: The sidecar does not carry enough information to determine the total readout time. Either TotalReadoutTime must be given directly, or EffectiveEchoSpacing must be given so it can be derived.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error of missing metadata. It is not that a value is wrong, but that neither of the two accepted ways of stating the readout time is present.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Readout time determines how far susceptibility distortion displaces the image along the phase-encoding axis. Without it, distortion correction cannot compute the size of the correction, only its direction.
common_causes: The conversion did not derive the value, which happens when the source data does not expose the parameters it is computed from.
The field was removed during anonymisation or sidecar editing.
The sidecar was written from a template that omitted it.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add either TotalReadoutTime or EffectiveEchoSpacing to the sidecar, in seconds. Both can be derived from the acquisition parameters: the echo spacing, the number of phase-encoding lines and the parallel imaging acceleration factor. These are available from the scanner protocol, and many conversion tools will compute them if given the original source files rather than already-converted images.

title: WARNING TRIGGER_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH
summary: TRIGGER_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH: The TriggerChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type TRIG in the associated channels.tsv file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code TRIGGER_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH (warning). The TriggerChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type TRIG in the associated channels.tsv file. When the file's suffix is eeg and type(sidecar.TriggerChannelCount) != "null" and associations.channels.type, it requires that sidecar.TriggerChannelCount == the number of associations.channels.type, "TRIG". Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named TriggerChannelCountReq in the BIDS schema. It concerns eeg data.

requirements.message: The TriggerChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type TRIG in the associated channels.tsv file.

issue.message:
The TriggerChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels
with type TRIG in the associated channels.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: The TriggerChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is TRIG. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many TRIG channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset is still valid BIDS, but one of the two statements about the recording is wrong and downstream software may read either of them. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while TriggerChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original TriggerChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar TriggerChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "trig" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as TRIG.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals TRIG. If that number is right, set TriggerChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

title: WARNING UNKNOWN_BIDS_VERSION
summary: UNKNOWN_BIDS_VERSION: The BIDSVersion field of 'dataset_description.json' does not match a known release. The BIDS Schema used for validation may be out of date.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code UNKNOWN_BIDS_VERSION (warning). The BIDSVersion field of 'dataset_description.json' does not match a known release. The BIDS Schema used for validation may be out of date. When path == '/dataset_description.json', it requires that [json.BIDSVersion] shares a value with schema.meta.versions. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named UnknownVersion in the BIDS schema. It concerns dataset data.

requirements.message: The BIDSVersion field of 'dataset_description.json' does not match a known release. The BIDS Schema used for validation may be out of date.

issue.message:
The BIDSVersion field of 'dataset_description.json' does not match a known release.
The BIDS Schema used for validation may be out of date.

ai_enrichment.description: The BIDSVersion field of dataset_description.json does not name a known BIDS release, so the validator fell back to its own default schema version.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. Validation still ran, but against a version the dataset did not ask for, so the results describe compliance with a different version of the standard than the one declared.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: BIDS evolves. A rule that is required in one version may be recommended in another, and suffixes and entities are added over time. Validating against the wrong version can report problems that do not exist under the declared version, or miss ones that do.
common_causes: A typo in the version string, or a missing patch component.
A development or pre-release version string that names no published release.
A version newer than the validator knows about.
The field left as a placeholder.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Set BIDSVersion to a published BIDS release that the dataset actually conforms to, written as a plain version number. If the dataset was built against a development version of the standard, decide which released version to declare before sharing it, since repositories and tools generally expect a stable one. If the version is simply newer than the validator, update the validator.

title: WARNING UNKNOWN_PUPIL_SIZE
summary: UNKNOWN_PUPIL_SIZE: The pupil_size description in the JSON sidecar does not clearly indicate whether the size is area or diameter.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code UNKNOWN_PUPIL_SIZE (warning). The pupil_size description in the JSON sidecar does not clearly indicate whether the size is area or diameter. When the file's suffix is physio and sidecar.PhysioType == "eyetrack" and columns.pupil_size, it requires that match(sidecar.pupil_size.Description, '.*(area|diameter).*'). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named PupilSizeDescription in the BIDS schema. It concerns eyetrack data.

requirements.message: The pupil_size description in the JSON sidecar does not clearly indicate whether the size is area or diameter.

issue.message: The `pupil_size` description in the JSON sidecar does not clearly indicate whether the size is area or diameter.

ai_enrichment.description: The description of the pupil_size column in the JSON sidecar does not make clear whether the values are pupil area or pupil diameter.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The data is present and usable; what is missing is the statement of which quantity it represents.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Area and diameter are related by a square, so treating one as the other distorts every pupillometric measure. Eye trackers differ in which they report, and some can be configured either way, so the quantity cannot be inferred from the equipment alone.
common_causes: The description was left generic, saying only that the column holds pupil size.
The tracker's own terminology was copied without resolving which quantity it means.
The recording mode was not documented at acquisition time.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Write the description of the pupil_size column to say explicitly whether the values are area or diameter, and give the units. Determine which from the eye tracker's configuration for this recording rather than from its default, since the setting is often changed per experiment.

title: ERROR VOLUME_COUNT_MISMATCH
summary: VOLUME_COUNT_MISMATCH: The number of volumes in this scan does not match the number of volumes in the associated '.bvec' and '.bval' files.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code VOLUME_COUNT_MISMATCH (error). The number of volumes in this scan does not match the number of volumes in the associated '.bvec' and '.bval' files. When [suffix] shares a value with ["dwi", "epi"] and "bval" in associations and "bvec" in associations and type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that associations.bval.n_cols == nifti_header.dim[4] and associations.bvec.n_cols == nifti_header.dim[4]. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named DWIVolumeCount in the BIDS schema. It concerns dwi data.

requirements.message: The number of volumes in this scan does not match the number of volumes in the associated '.bvec' and '.bval' files.

issue.message:
The number of volumes in this scan does not match the number of volumes in the
associated '.bvec' and '.bval' files.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of volumes in a diffusion image does not match the number of entries in its .bval and .bvec files.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Each volume needs exactly one b-value and one gradient direction, so the three counts must agree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: If the counts differ, the pairing between volumes and gradients is wrong from the point of the discrepancy onward. Every volume after it is analysed with another volume's gradient, which corrupts the fit without producing any obvious failure.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image, for example corrupted ones dropped during quality control, without the corresponding entries being removed from the gradient files.
The acquisition was stopped early, so fewer volumes were saved than the gradient table describes.
The gradient files belong to a different run, which is easy when several diffusion runs share a scheme.
Two runs were concatenated but only one gradient table was carried over.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image, the values in the .bval and the columns in the .bvec. If volumes were dropped, remove the same positions from both gradient files, which requires knowing which volumes were removed. If the gradient files belong to another run, find the correct ones. Do not trim the gradient files from the end to match the count unless you know the missing volumes were the last ones.

title: ERROR VOLUME_TIMING_AND_DELAY_TIME_MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE
summary: VOLUME_TIMING_AND_DELAY_TIME_MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE: The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' for this file are mutually exclusive. To specify acquisition duration, use 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming'.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code VOLUME_TIMING_AND_DELAY_TIME_MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE (error). The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' for this file are mutually exclusive. To specify acquisition duration, use 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming'. When [suffix] shares a value with ["asl", "bold"] and the file is a NIfTI image (.nii or .nii.gz) and type(sidecar.VolumeTiming) != "null" and type(sidecar.RepetitionTime) == "null", it requires that type(sidecar.DelayTime) == "null". Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named VolumeTimingDelayTimeMutex in the BIDS schema. It concerns func data.

requirements.message: The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' for this file are mutually exclusive. To specify acquisition duration, use 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming'.

issue.message:
The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' for this file are mutually exclusive.
To specify acquisition duration, use 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming'.

ai_enrichment.description: VolumeTiming and DelayTime are both present in the same sidecar. BIDS treats them as mutually exclusive ways of describing the same acquisition timing, so only one may be given.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. It is not that one of the two values is wrong; it is that giving both leaves the file describing its timing twice, with no rule saying which description wins.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Downstream software has to choose one. Different tools choose differently, so the same dataset yields different timing depending on what reads it. Removing the redundant field is what makes the timing unambiguous.
common_causes: A conversion wrote every timing field it could derive from the source data, without applying the standard's exclusivity rules.
A field was added by hand to an existing sidecar that already described its timing another way.
A sidecar was merged from two sources, each using a different convention.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: DelayTime describes the gap between the end of one volume's acquisition and the start of the next within a regular repetition time, so it belongs with RepetitionTime rather than with VolumeTiming. When volume times are listed individually, the delays are already implied by the list. Decide which description matches the acquisition and delete the other field from the sidecar. Do not leave both with the intention of being thorough: in this case, more metadata is less information.

ai_enrichment.description: VolumeTiming and RepetitionTime are both present in the same sidecar. BIDS treats them as mutually exclusive ways of describing the same acquisition timing, so only one may be given.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. It is not that one of the two values is wrong; it is that giving both leaves the file describing its timing twice, with no rule saying which description wins.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Downstream software has to choose one. Different tools choose differently, so the same dataset yields different timing depending on what reads it. Removing the redundant field is what makes the timing unambiguous.
common_causes: A conversion wrote every timing field it could derive from the source data, without applying the standard's exclusivity rules.
A field was added by hand to an existing sidecar that already described its timing another way.
A sidecar was merged from two sources, each using a different convention.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: RepetitionTime describes a regular acquisition where volumes are evenly spaced, and is the right choice for most functional runs. VolumeTiming lists the time of every volume individually and exists for sparse or irregular designs where no single interval applies. Decide which description matches the acquisition and delete the other field from the sidecar. Do not leave both with the intention of being thorough: in this case, more metadata is less information.

ai_enrichment.description: VolumeTiming is present, but neither FrameAcquisitionDuration nor SliceTiming is given. VolumeTiming states when each volume started and needs one of those two to say how long each volume took.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error of incompleteness rather than contradiction. VolumeTiming alone describes only the start of each volume.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: In a sparse design, the gap between volumes is deliberate and the acquisition occupies only part of it. Without a duration, software cannot tell how much of each interval contains data, which is exactly the information a sparse design exists to control.
common_causes: A sparse or clustered-volume acquisition was described with VolumeTiming, and the companion field was not added.
RepetitionTime was replaced with VolumeTiming during a correction, and the duration that RepetitionTime had implied was not supplied.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add FrameAcquisitionDuration, giving how long the acquisition of a single volume takes, or add SliceTiming, which gives the acquisition time of each slice and therefore implies the duration. Take the value from the acquisition protocol. If the run is in fact evenly spaced, the simpler description is RepetitionTime alone, without VolumeTiming.

title: ERROR VOLUME_TIMING_NOT_MONOTONICALLY_INCREASING
summary: VOLUME_TIMING_NOT_MONOTONICALLY_INCREASING: 'VolumeTiming' is not monotonically increasing.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code VOLUME_TIMING_NOT_MONOTONICALLY_INCREASING (error). 'VolumeTiming' is not monotonically increasing. When the file belongs to the mri modality and sidecar.VolumeTiming != null, it requires that allequal(sorted(sidecar.VolumeTiming), sidecar.VolumeTiming). Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named VolumeTimingNotMonotonicallyIncreasing in the BIDS schema. It concerns mri data.

requirements.message: 'VolumeTiming' is not monotonically increasing.

issue.message: 'VolumeTiming' is not monotonically increasing.

ai_enrichment.description: The values in VolumeTiming are not in increasing order. VolumeTiming lists the acquisition time of each volume, so the times must increase.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Volumes were acquired one after another, so a list of their times that goes backwards, or repeats, cannot describe a real acquisition.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The order of VolumeTiming establishes which entry belongs to which volume. A list that is out of order either mispairs times with volumes or contains wrong values, and both corrupt any analysis that models time.
common_causes: The list was assembled from values sorted by something other than time.
Duplicate entries, often from concatenating two runs.
A negative or zero value inserted as a placeholder.
Volumes were removed from the middle of the list without their times being removed.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Inspect the array and find where it stops increasing, which usually identifies the cause immediately. Verify the times against the acquisition log rather than simply sorting the list, since sorting produces an increasing sequence that may still pair the wrong time with each volume.
